nodes.name: NF cleaning and NiMoO4_xH2O hydrothermal
nodes.procedure: A piece of bare NF (4 cm²) was ultrasonically washed under conditions of 3 M HCl, ethanol, and DI water. Subsequently, the mixture consisted of 30 ml of DI water, 1.2 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, and 0.3 mmol of (NH4)6Mo7O24·2H2O was stirred for 10 min in the Teflon autoclave. Next, the cleaning NF was immersed into the above solution and kept at 150°C for 6 hours. After the temperature was cooled down, the NiMoO4·xH2O precursor was rinsed by DI water and dried in air.

nodes.name: NiMoO4 electrooxidation to Mo-NiOOH
nodes.procedure: The Mo-NiOOH catalyst was synthesized by a chronoamperometry method under a three-electrode system in 1.0 M KOH at a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² for 20 min, in which the NiMoO4·xH2O precursor (1.0 cm²) was used as the working electrode, the graphite rod was used as the counter electrode, and the Hg/HgO electrode served as the reference electrode.

nodes.name: Mo-NiOOH spontaneous reduction
nodes.procedure: The synthesized Mo-NiOOH catalyst was immersed into a 1.0 M KOH electrolyte containing 0.1 M EG under stirring, and black Mo-NiOOH was spontaneously reduced to green Mo-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.source_text: The synthesized Mo-NiOOH catalyst was immersed into a 1.0 M KOH electrolyte containing 0.1 M EG under stirring...

nodes.name: Ni(OH)₂ NSs hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: The mixed solution for the hydrothermal treatment consisted of 30 ml of DI water, 2 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 10 mmol of urea, and 4 mmol of NH₄F was stirred for 10 min in the Teflon autoclave. Subsequently, a piece of cleaning NF (4 cm²) was immersed into the above solution and kept at 120°C for 6 hours. After the temperature cooled down, the green Ni(OH)₂ catalyst was rinsed by DI water and dried in air overnight.

nodes.name: PET upcycling product separation
nodes.procedure: After PET hydrolysate electrolysis, 100 ml of FA (88 wt%) was slowly added into the electrolyte to adjust the pH to 3.0 under stirring. After the temperature was cooled down, PTA precipitations were filtrated and washed for several times. Afterward, the filtrate was concentrated at 60°C under stirring for 3 days, with a daily supplement of 20 ml of FA (88 wt%) until the crystals precipitated in the solution. Afterward, the hot solution was cooled at 4°C for 12 hours. Last, the KDF product was obtained through filtering the initially precipitated crystals and then evaporating the remaining filtrate.

nodes.description: EGOR LSV half-cell performance in alkaline water/seawater media

electrolyte.value: 1.0 M KOH + 0.5 M EG and alkaline seawater

nodes.source_text: Half-cell EGOR performances under alkaline water/seawater media were evaluated through a three-electrode system. As shown in figs. S21 and S22, linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves that exhibit Mo-Ni(OH)₂ only requires 1.38 and 1.41 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) to drive 100 and 300 mA cm⁻²... The high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) chromatograms demonstrate that the highest faradic efficiency (FE; 95.8%) with selectivity (97.7%) is obtained at 1.55 V versus RHE
The Mo-Ni(OH)₂ shows an impressive stability with negligible deactivation over 300 hours under a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² in a flow electrolyzer
NiO/NiMoOₓ only requires overpotentials of 75 and 126 mV to drive 100 and 300 mA cm⁻². Tafel slope of NiO/NiMoOₓ (40.5 mV dec⁻¹)
the reconstructed *OH-NiO/NiMoOₓ catalyst exhibits excellent HER stability for over 350 hours under a current density of 100 mA cm⁻² with nearly 100% FE

nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscope (TEM) image with the selected-area electron diffraction reveals typical lattice mismatching of the amorphous phase (fig. S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows NiMoO₄·xH₂O precursor (PDF #12-0348) transforms into nickel hydroxide phase (PDF #14-0117).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The x-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern (fig. S12) indicates that the NiMoO₄·xH₂O precursor (PDF #12-0348) transforms into nickel hydroxide phase (PDF #14-0117).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p XPS spectra show Mo-Ni(OH)₂ has lower Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ ratio than Ni(OH)₂ (fig. S15).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ni 2p spectra indicate that Mo-Ni(OH)₂ has a lower ratio of Ni³⁺/Ni²⁺ (fig. S15).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows large amounts of MoO₄²⁻ ions dissolve from catalyst during electrooxidation (table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) result that large amounts of MoO₄²⁻ ions dissolve from the catalyst during the electrooxidation process (table S1 and fig. S16).

nodes.characterization_summary: Negative shift of Ni K-edge XANES spectra of Mo-Ni(OH)₂ indicates lower average valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The negative shift of Ni K-edge x-ray absorption near edge structure spectra of Mo-Ni(OH)₂ represents a lower average valence state (figs. S18 to S20).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS shows Ni-Ni scattering at 2.48 Å and Ni-O coordination at 2.08 Å (table S2).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform extended x-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra in R-space show intensity maximum of Ni-Ni scattering at 2.48Å and Ni-O coordination at 2.08Å (table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Zeta potential of Mo-Ni(OH)₂ is -6.24 mV vs -0.79 mV for Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a lower zeta potential of Mo-Ni(OH)₂ (-6.24 mV) than that of Ni(OH)₂ (-0.79 mV) implies better chlorine resistance of the former (fig. S39).

nodes.characterization_summary: Higher Cdl of Mo-Ni(OH)₂ indicates larger ECSA than Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: increasing double-layer capacitance (Cdl) of Mo-Ni(OH)₂ for EGOR implies the larger electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) (figs. S40 and S41).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman of Mo-NiOOH shows Ni³⁺-O stretching peaks at 476 and 553 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Raman spectra of Mo-NiOOH, two strong doublet peaks at 476 and 553 cm⁻¹ belong to the Ni³⁺-O stretching vibration (Fig. 3, A and B).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FTIR shows glyoxal peak at 1068 cm⁻¹ and formate bands at 1230, 1326, 1412, 1585 cm⁻¹; no CO intermediates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the absorption band at 1068 cm⁻¹ is assigned to the aldehyde stretching of glyoxal... Representative absorption bands of formate at 1230, 1326, 1412, and 1585 cm⁻¹ belong to the C-O stretching, the antisymmetric and symmetric stretching of COO⁻, and the C-O asymmetric stretching.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability SEM shows retained nanorod structure of Mo-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Mo-Ni(OH)₂ catalyst shows high catalytic stability for EGOR, as confirmed by the retained nanorod structure in the SEM result (fig. S44).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability XRD shows nearly unchanged (101) plane of Ni(OH)₂ at 0.233 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the almost unchanged lattice fringe of 0.233 nm assigned to the (101) plane for Ni(OH)₂ in the XRD and TEM results (figs. S46 and S47) after long-term EGOR.
